accuracy.evidence: Checked against the National Curriculum in England English Appendix 2 (Year 2: adjectives in expanded noun phrases, suffix -ly to turn adjectives into adverbs), Appendix 1 Years 3–4 (-ly spelling: add -ly; consonant + y changes y to i as in happily; -le becomes -ly as in gently) and CCSS L.2.1e (choose between adjectives and adverbs by what is modified). Linking-verb rule (the cat is quiet) and flat adverbs fast, hard, early and well as the adverb of good match the Cambridge Grammar of English entries. Flat-adverb informal uses (sing loud, come quick) were removed from the fix-it lines so no sentence marked wrong is defensible in standard usage.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented Year 2–3 errors: adjective after an action verb (gap step Sam runs quick; fix lines spoke polite, walk careful; challenge 'verb'), hypercorrect -ly after a linking verb (The sun was brightly, The cat is quiet prediction, challenge 'is', mastery m8), spelling slips happyly, gentlely, easyly (step 2 feedback, challenge 'spell', p3, m3), judging by the ending so friendly and lovely look like adverbs (step 5 prediction, challenge 'ly', m1) and missing no-ly adverbs fast, hard, well (step 5 sort, m4, m6, challenge 'well').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagadjadv is built on what a describing word attaches to: an arrow from the coloured word to the noun or verb it describes, an ending tile chosen by the root's last letters, a gap whose neighbour (runs versus is) decides the form, and a sort where the same word (fast, hard) lands in both boxes. flagnv sorts nouns and verbs, flagnph builds noun phrases and flagadvl moves fronted adverbials; none links modifiers to heads. The lab_distinct gate passed under 30% similarity to every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the rule by acting: tapping dog for slowly is refused because slowly tells how something happens, dragging +ly onto happy is refused with the y to i reason, dropping quietly after is is refused because is is not an action, and sorting friendly as an adverb is refused because it tells about the cat. Each completion line restates the rule just used (adjectives point at nouns, adverbs at verbs).

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each have a tempting wrong option that the lab disproves: slowly tells about the dog (step 1, disproved by the arrow landing on walks), happyly (step 2, disproved when only y → ily is accepted), and friendly is an adverb because it ends in ly (step 5, disproved by the sort). Step 3 also asks The cat is ___ where quietly is the tempting hypercorrection.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Every wrong challenge choice has its own message keyed to the slip: 'is' (adverb after a linking verb), 'both' (thinks either form fits), 'verb' (adjective after ran), 'plain' (quickely), 'ly' and 'noverb' (silly), 'spell' (easyly, easly), 'well' (good or goodly for how she plays), 'head' and 'alone' (softly attached to He or to nothing). Six questions rotate so a retry gives a new item.

readability.evidence: Kid text measures FK grade 1.4 against the family target of 5, in short sentences that introduce noun, verb, adjective and adverb one at a time with an example each. Lab prompts are short (Gap 1 of 5: drag the right word in). Adult text is FK 9.9 against the 10 target and uses the curriculum terms suffix, root word, linking verb.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one idea: adjective on a noun, adverb on a verb, the -ly spelling rules, then choosing by job with the friendly and fast traps. The content gate found no banned phrases and explanation overlap is under 12%. Every lab feedback line gives the specific reason for that word, for example 'was is not an action. The word tells us about the sun: bright.'

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark for all 6 steps: word tiles scale to fit one line at 390 px, the ending tiles are three equal 54 px targets across the width, gap cards sit side by side at about 150 px, bin labels were shortened to 'Adjective: a thing' and 'Adverb: how' after the first pass clipped, the hint lines shrink to fit, and full stops now draw in the theme text colour so they show in dark mode.

accessibility.evidence: The walkthrough gate completed every task with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) reported no violations in light or dark. Every drag or tap has a full-size button equivalent with a spoken label (e.g. 'slow tells about dog', 'quick: + ly', 'Put quickly in the gap'), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with each feedback message.

sources: National Curriculum in England: English Appendix 2 Vocabulary, grammar and punctuation, Year 2 (adjectives, suffix -ly to turn adjectives into adverbs)
National Curriculum in England: English Appendix 1 Spelling, Years 3 and 4 (the suffix -ly: happily, gently)
Common Core State Standards ELA L.2.1e: use adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified
Cambridge Grammar of English (Carter and McCarthy): adverbs with the same form as adjectives (fast, hard, early) and well as the adverb of good
